newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: "Evita" opens with minor incidents in Argentina.
newsitem.headline: "Evita" opens with minor incidents in Argentina.

text.p: Police tightened security at theatres showing "Evita" on Friday after the controversial film opened in Argentina to pesticide attacks.
Three movie houses had to be evacuated when pesticide spray devices were set off as the musical based on the life of Eva Peron and starring pop idol Madonna opened on Thursday.

Viewers leaving one of the cinemas in Buenos Aires also ran into Peronist Youth demonstrators loudly protesting the film's portrayal of Evita as a woman who used her sex appeal to gain political power.

In La Plata, capital of Buenos Aires province, left-wing militants tore down posters advertising the film and pelted a ticket office. In the province of Mendoza two movie theatres screening "Evita" were sprayed with paint overnight.
Vice President Carlos Ruckauf, of the ruling Peronist Party, repeated his call on Friday for a boycott of the movie. "I hope they make a loss here," he told reporters.
But the state news agency Telam said more people showed up to see "Evita" than normally go to the movies on Thursdays, and local media said audiences clapped at the end of the film.
Artists and politicians who attended Monday's premiere criticised the film as historically inaccurate and slanderous.
Evita, the wife of populist leader Juan Domingo Peron, championed Argentina's working class and died of cancer in 1952 while she was the country's first lady.
She is still revered by many Peronists as a saint for her charity work and defence of the rights of workers, who she referred to affectionately as "my shirtless ones."
